title: Slow-cooker Boston baked beans
subtitle: American-style slow-cooked beans with treacle and salt pork
excerpt: Haricot beans cooked with back bacon, black treacle, and dark brown sugar in a deep, smoky sauce. The American original made easy in a slow cooker.
sourceNotes: Boston baked beans are a traditional New England American dish, originally cooked for hours in a ceramic pot by Puritan settlers. The combination of beans, pork, black treacle, and mustard is documented in American cookbooks from the 19th century including the Boston Cook Book by Mary J. Lincoln (1884).

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. The sauce thickens further on freezing. Reheat on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: A classic batch-cook recipe. Makes 6 large portions and keeps in the fridge for 5 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Better after a night in the fridge. The treacle flavour deepens as the beans sit.

content.text: The difference between British baked beans and Boston baked beans is the treacle. The American version uses black treacle, which gives the sauce a dark, almost bittersweet depth that is very different from the bright tomato sweetness of the British tin. Back bacon replaces the traditional salt pork and works very well.

These beans need a long cook to become the real thing. Eight hours is not too many. The longer they cook, the more the sauce concentrates and the deeper the flavour becomes. Do not open the lid more than once or twice during cooking.
Serve with cornbread, over jacket potatoes, or as a side dish with sausages.

items.prepNote: taste before adding; bacon adds salt

content.text: Add {{haricot-beans}} of drained haricot beans to the slow cooker. Add {{back-bacon}} of back bacon pieces, {{onion}} diced onion, and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic. Pour in {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes and {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree. Add {{black-treacle}} of black treacle, {{dark-brown-sugar}} of dark brown sugar, {{mustard-powder}} of mustard powder, and {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce. Stir everything together.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 7 to 8 hours. Stir once or twice if possible. The sauce should be thick and dark when done. Taste before adding {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt; the bacon will have contributed salt during cooking.

rows.cause: Two tablespoons of black treacle can be intense in a small volume of liquid.
rows.fix: Stir in an extra tablespoon of dark brown sugar and a splash of hot water. Cook for 15 more minutes. Next time use one tablespoon of treacle and one of molasses.

rows.cause: The tinned tomatoes added more liquid than the beans absorbed.
rows.fix: Cook on HIGH with the lid off for 30 minutes. Or stir in a tablespoon of tomato puree.

rows.cause: Tinned beans cook through quickly and can begin to lose their shape after 8 hours.
rows.fix: This is fine if you want a thick, mashed-style result. Check at 6 hours next time for beans that hold their shape.

rows.cause: The back bacon added more salt than expected.
rows.fix: Stir in a tablespoon of apple juice or a splash of water to dilute. Next time, rinse the bacon before using or reduce the salt addition.

content.text: Boston baked beans are one of the oldest American recipes still in regular use. They were a Puritan staple cooked in a sealed pot over embers from Saturday evening for a Sunday meal. The sweet, treacly, slow-cooked style became a defining dish of New England. The slow cooker replaces the sealed pot and the embers with something far more convenient.
